Maximum Demand Definition and Related Terms

The maximum demand definition in electrical engineering is the highest average load, in kW or kVA, that an installation draws over a set demand interval during a billing or study period. Energy meters usually average over 15 or 30 minute intervals, so a short motor starting surge does not set maximum demand, but a sustained peak does. It is always lower than or equal to the connected load.

TermDefinitionTypical value
Connected loadSum of all nameplate ratingsLargest figure
Maximum demandHighest interval average load actually drawnLess than connected load
Demand factorMaximum demand divided by connected load1 or less
Diversity factorSum of individual maximum demands divided by system maximum demand1 or more
Load factorAverage load divided by peak load over a periodBetween 0 and 1

Example: a plant with 500 kW connected load and a demand factor of 0.7 has a maximum demand of 500 × 0.7 = 350 kW. If its average load over the month is 245 kW, the load factor is 245 ÷ 350 = 0.7. The utility bills the 350 kW peak, so lowering short sustained peaks reduces the demand charge even when energy use stays the same.
